reading: The interior of the rectangular outline is filled with the colour of the small loose object, and that loose object is erased to background.
verb: fill frame with loose piece's colour

slots.region: interior of the one rectangular outline (frame)

why: the frame interior equals the loose object's colour; the loose object's cells become background; the outline is unchanged

reading: The input is scaled up by a factor equal to the number of non-background colours; then colour-2 diagonals run from each corner of the scaled square block outward until they hit a non-background cell or the grid edge.
verb: scale up and draw corner diagonals

slots.factor: number of distinct non-background colours in the input
slots.lines: diagonal rays of colour 2 from the four outer corners of the interior square block
slots.stop: first non-background cell or grid border

why: output = input scaled by k (k = colour count) plus 2-diagonals from the block's corners on background only

reading: Each coloured cell (all at odd row/column positions) becomes a 4x4 block in a 20x20 output: output cell (Y,X) takes input cell (2*(Y div 4)+1, 2*(X div 4)+1).

slots.sample: input cells at odd rows and odd columns (a 5x5 sub-grid)
slots.scale: each sampled cell enlarged to a 4x4 block

why: output is the odd-position 5x5 sample of the input enlarged x4

reading: A full cross of one colour splits the grid; the shape in the top-left quadrant is recoloured to the cross colour and reflected into all four quadrants (left-right and top-bottom mirrors), with the cross removed.

slots.unit: top-left panel cut by the separator cross
slots.layout: 2x2 arrangement: unit, horizontal mirror, vertical mirror, both

why: output is 2h x 2w, symmetric both ways, each quadrant the recoloured unit or its mirror

reading: The two colours of the input are swapped (background becomes the colour and vice versa), and the result is tiled 2x2.

slots.unit: input with its two colours swapped

why: every 2x2 block of the output is the colour-inverted input

reading: The colour-8 shape is cut out as a 3x3 box (its 3 columns, the 3 rows ending at its bottom row) and repeated side by side once for each colour-4 marker cell.
verb: crop shape and repeat per marker

slots.unit: 3x3 box around the 8-shape (bottom-aligned when the shape is 2 rows)
slots.layout: copies in one row, left to right

why: output is 3 x 3n with n = number of 4-markers, every block equal to the cropped shape

reading: Vertical colour-8 bars have lengths 2,4,6,8,10; one bar has half of it coloured 9. The 9 half is removed (back to 8) and instead the next-longer bar (length + 2) gets the same half (top or bottom) coloured 9.

slots.target: the bar whose length is the source length + 2
slots.marking: same end (top/bottom) half of the target recoloured 9; source restored to 8

why: exactly the source's 9 cells revert to 8 and the target's matching half becomes 9

reading: The 3x3 input is placed into a 9x9 grid at the blocks where the input has its least frequent colour; other blocks are empty.
why: block (i,j) holds the input iff input cell (i,j) has the colour with the fewest pixels, else it is all 0
invariants: the unit is the unchanged input

reading: The coloured stripes at the top are reflected to the bottom of the grid about the horizontal centre line.
why: output is symmetric about the horizontal mid-line; input cells are kept

reading: The single marker cell is extended into a filled rectangle spanning from the marker to the grid corner nearest to it, in the marker's colour.

new_rows.name: corner_rect
new_rows.datalog:
h(max(Y)) :- px(Y, X, C).
w(max(X)) :- px(Y, X, C).
m(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C).
rowok(Y) :- m(MY, MX), h(H), px(Y, X, C), D = MY + MY, D <= H, Y <= MY.
rowok(Y) :- m(MY, MX), h(H), px(Y, X, C), D = MY + MY, D > H, Y >= MY.
colok(X) :- m(MY, MX), w(W), px(Y, X, C), D = MX + MX, D <= W, X <= MX.
colok(X) :- m(MY, MX), w(W), px(Y, X, C), D = MX + MX, D > W, X >= MX.
corner_rect(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), rowok(Y), colok(X).

why: every cell of the box between the marker and its nearest grid corner takes the marker colour; all other cells stay background
